keyFindings.description: pointerPairs (:246) accepts a pointer whenever its block id is a node id, but nodes are uniqueBlocks' first holder of each id. So a typed block that is a later holder of a repeated id (which a rendered version can carry, pmdoc/block_ids.go) has its pointers written as edges from the first holder, possibly a paragraph. Its pointed count also subtracts the first holder's real mention of that target. Meanwhile the later holder's own text mention goes to its innermost node and is not subtracted. Mentions never attribute by id this way. Emit pointers only from the first holder of each id, as uniqueBlocks does, or check that the node's type is the pointer's BlockType, and add a test.

refuseBlockPointers (:263-305) queries document_blocks and copies the first-holder rule of refs.uniqueBlocks without its id checks. Every other document_blocks read is in refs. Move the type resolution into refs, reusing uniqueBlocks, so the refusal and the index use one node rule. It is fixed in this push with finding 1, since both are the same rule.
